I am not sure if this is compatible, but you are welcome to try it:
GitHub - movinglinguini/pixijs-grid: A utility for creating grids in pixijs
A utility for creating grids in pixijs. Contribute to movinglinguini/pixijs-grid development by creating an account on GitHub.
github.com
If you are looking to do it yourself, I would draw the border with .drawRect(x, y, width, height) where x/y is the starting point and width/height is, well, the wdith and height of your rectangle.
Every child (or new child) that you create must be referenced by their own id or by a name that you designate.
When you use .clear(), it only clears the contents of that specific child.
Using .destroy() will remove the contents as well as the object which means you have to create a new graphic.
If you use the same name for several children in your scene, it will try to look for the first one it can find and only return that, assuming you are looking in the correct property/object.
Be sure to remember where you place them and if you are naming them, remember to give them unique names/ids.
Otherwise, they are stored as an array, typically under the .children property (in the order that it was added).

That means you have to be able to find the child specifically that you add.
So if you added a new graphic at SceneManager._scene._spriteset, you have to reference it first before you can clear/destroy.
Let's say you added 3 graphics. In order to find them easier, you have to name them. For this example, we will call them 'graph1', 'graph2', and 'graph3'. All three are added to the spriteset.
To find and clear/destroy a specific graph, you need to find it with the getChildByName() function. So, to get graph2 inside of spriteset and clear it without touching graph1 or graph3, we do:
JavaScript:
SceneManager._scene._spriteset.getChildByName('graph2').clear();
It is important that you either know where they are added as a child or name them so you can use the function above to get them. Again, naming them with the same name will make it much harder to organize.
Unless I am misunderstanding what you are after?
When dealing with all these graphics, I like to put then into a texture so I can create a sprite and deal with them from there as a set. But that is another part of PIXI that you will need to explore (there are also containers as well which are display objects that can hold the sprites, etc.).
I do recommend checking the PIXI.js documentation for your specific version since it can be much more helpful to test and run things yourself.

g.name('test1');

new PIXI.Graphics()
  .beginFill(0xffffff)
  .drawCircle(100,100,100)
  .endFill();
g.addChild(h);  // Add the child to g instead of spriteset
By adding the other child to g which is named '
test

To use it externally after defining it, you will need to reference the bitmap.
Add this to the list right before you add the child (use spr or sprite, whatever you referenced ans also include the container):
JavaScript:
spr.name = 'house';
container.name = 'container';
Then, to use clearRect, do:
JavaScript:
const s = SceneManager._scene._spriteset.getChildByName('container');
const spr = s.getChildByName('house');
spr.bitmap.clearRect(0, 0, 300, 300);
The goal is to find the child under the property/object of where you added it. If you added it in spriteset, you need to find the child under that object first. Since there is a container, you also have to find that part.
Thing to consider: keep in mind that if you run this script call multiple times, the game will create multiple children with the same name so you will have to delete them all separately.
Finding the child by their name will only return the first name that matches. Check the console for all children added to the scene.
